# Contact and candidate selection observations

`contact.tsv` records actual public `Organism.contact` and `World.checkHit` operations.
It does not call a method named `touchEffects`.
The contact method internally invokes original pretouch, reaction, friendship, C1, C2, and physical helpers.
Two source runs and the bundled JAR produced identical bytes.
All five compiled helper classes match across backends.

The fixed scope contains 61 cases, 186 snapshots, 566 actor views, and four discovered newborns.
There are 64 actual tree builds, 49 direct contacts, and twelve World candidate checks.
Each actor view contains all 154 organism observation fields.

## Comparison contract

The ledger, typed inputs, and exclusions precede Rust replay.
Compare nongeometric float bits, gases, statistics, RNG, integers, ARGB, reactions, endpoints, bounds, identities, and ordering exactly.
Only organism `_m`, `_m1`, `_m2`, `_mass`, and `_I` retain the established geometry allowance.
For finite geometry, use `1e-10 * max(1, abs(expected))`.
Classify geometric NaN and signed infinity explicitly.
No contact velocity, energy, Boolean, or identity receives an additional allowance.

Organism exclusions are `_world` and `_visibleWorld`.
World exclusions are `_visibleWorld`, `inCorridors`, `outCorridors`, and `_corridorexists`.
Selection remains callback-routing metadata.
Y records describe genotype reachability through actual holders and explicit supplied recipes.
Every Y scope is observable; there are no rejected candidate objects or discarded genotype observations.
All remaining observations are comparison obligations.
These exclusions do not establish UI or corridor behavior.

## Protocol

The helper reuses the existing Cooperative and Coral dynamic protocol.
It adds the approved meanings for B outcomes.

| Row | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| C/U/I | Case, all primitive settings, and ordered typed controls |
| G/N input | Explicit supplied genome recipes and gene fields |
| A | Actual pasted and added actor inputs |
| K | Original operation and explicit arguments |
| B | Actual direct-contact Boolean or World return identity |
| J | Actual tree insertion identity and current rectangle |
| D | Newly discovered World member identity, actual ID, and genotype reference |
| P | Snapshot ordering marker |
| O/H | Full organism fields and three whole-genome holders |
| W/V | World getters and all fifteen World instance fields |
| Q | Actual frozen-tree query identities and order |
| S/T | All 52 statistics fields and 49 getters |
| Y/G/N | Genotype reachability and full observed genome/gene state |
| R | Nonconsuming peek at the real Java RNG |
| E | Case boundary |

K records use `contact,victim,killer`, `checkHit,victim,~`, or the existing `build_tree,victim,roles` arguments.
B records have four columns: `B,stage,operation,value`.
For contact, value is the original returned `true` or `false`.
For checkHit, value is the actual returned actor identity `victim`, or null `~`.
The source returns the held actor rather than its colliding peer.
No numeric-ID lookup constructs that result.
D discovery uses Java object identity and actual World membership order.
It never creates an actor from an expected snapshot.

## Construction and labelled geometry

Each case resets actual defaults and records all 147 mutable primitive Utils settings.
Initial organism attempts are zero; initial oxygen is `1000`.
Mutation bounds are `0..10000`; meta mutation is zero.
GREEN selection weight is seven; other selectable weights are zero.
The ordinary construction seed is `827364`.
EYE and selected OCHRE cases explicitly reset the real RNG through labelled `rng:seed` inputs.
No genesis or complete frame executes.

The helper constructs real VisibleWorld, World, GeneticCode, and Organism objects.
It invokes actual paste and World addition methods.
Selector, victim, and killer enter at `(1000,1000)`, `(3500,3500)`, and `(5000,5000)`.
Selector is selected before addition, avoiding unrelated MainWindow callbacks without substitutes.
Their initial numeric IDs are zero, one, and two.

Initial g0, g1, g2, and g3 are explicit recipes.
g4 is a real deep clone of g0.
Ordinary g0 and g1 use the case's actor and peer colors.
g2 is GREEN; g3 is WHITE.
Lengths begin at twelve; theta is `index * 0.25`; branches are zero.
Symmetry is one; mirror and mutation rate are zero.
Generation is 41, clade is `root`, and integer modifiers begin at one.
Targeted recipes supply additional genes and generation-battle, social, or peaceful flags.
All actual recipe fields appear in input G/N blocks before actor construction.

After placement, both contact actors receive explicit cached geometry.
Their integer and fractional centers become `(3500,3500)`.
Bounds become `(3494,3494,13,13)`.
Actor segments run from `(-5,0)` to `(5,0)` relative to the integer center.
Peer segments run from `(0,-5)` to `(0,5)`.
Physical lengths are two; photo markers are zero.
Mass and inertia are one; velocities, angular velocity, and growth changes begin zero.
The EYE entry flag begins false.
Every assignment is an ordered I input before any original contact call.

Ordinary contact actors receive energy 100, active/alive flags, unknown-parent IDs, and cleared relevant classifications and permissions.
Additional source states, reaction arrays, endpoint arrays, bounds, and nonfinite values are labelled inputs.
Arrays must match the actual segment count.
The source methods perform all physical calculations and biological effects.
The wrapper contains no copied collision, impulse, reaction, friendship, or reproduction formula.
The controlled caches do not claim natural frame reachability or a geometry rebuild.

## Distinct mechanisms

Physical cases cover exact length-one eligibility, short segments, bounding rejection, collinear endpoints, and degenerate lines.
They include signed determinants, wrapped integer endpoint addition, zero mass/inertia, and actor-only growth contributions.
The descending-pair case observes only the first physical segment pair.
Spike cases distinguish strict spike/spike ties, nonstrict other ties, existing photo-marker guards, and peer pretouch.

Actual TEAL braking observes impulse-before-reaction order.
Actual OCHRE velocity replacement observes impulse-before-biology order.
Dark mimicry changes current phenotype, photo marker, and generation permission before friendship and dispatch.
A separate peer mimic case observes reverse pretouch and reverse biological selection.
Friendship cases distinguish both parent directions, siblings, generation/sibling permissions, peaceful codes, social matching, and mismatched traits.
The sharing case performs a real friendly reaction followed by real altruist energy transfer.
Death cases observe cleared reverse permissions and reverse reactions after the original actor dies.

EYE cases use descending outer rays and ascending peer segments.
They include moving reactions without canreact, immobile braking, friendly braking, and false returns with actual side effects.
Entry flags, dead moving/immobile actors, zero/NaN/long lengths, short/NaN peer lengths, and translucent ARGB remain distinct.
A long EYE follows the regular physical path.

World cases observe exact self-identity filtering and distinct actors with equal numeric IDs.
They preserve alive-independent physical checks, strict rectangle overlap, and energy gates at the exact tolerance.
NaN energy skips candidate contact under the original comparison.
One case continues after EYE sensing returns false, then returns the held actor after a later physical collision.
Another case retains sensing effects while every candidate returns false.

The real PLAGUE contact creates one child.
The real YELLOW contact creates two children.
The real CORAL contact creates one transformation and kills its recipient.
Each child is discovered from actual World membership.
The source tree retains three original entries until an explicit subsequent rebuild.
The rebuild then includes the actual new members.
Full state, genotype holders, statistics, gas, tree queries, and RNG remain observed throughout.

## Isolation, preservation, and limits

Compile `tools/reference/ContactOracle.java` against each pinned backend.
Run `biogenesis.ContactOracle NEW_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` with the exact provenance arguments.
The helper checks four explicit profile roots through `toRealPath` before simulation access.
It refuses existing output directories and writes with `CREATE_NEW`.
Positive runs have a 120-second bound; compilation uses sixty seconds; negative runs use thirty seconds.
The existing runner cleans every owned process group.
Six actual guards cover each omitted root, an escaped preferences symlink, and existing-output preservation.

Final receipts remain under `.workflow-local/contact-oracle-7fcd9b1f/`.
All 74 original hash/size/mode pins, 159 compiled reference classes, and 35 prior TSV fixtures remain unchanged.
The initial compilation failure and its helper snapshot remain preserved.
The first successful 60-case capture also remains preserved.
Before Rust replay, a refinement activated real sharing and added one OCHRE ordering case.
Neither refinement used Rust outputs or followed a production mismatch.

These artifacts establish original method observations.
Rust comparison requires a separate strict replay and review.
They do not establish complete frame scheduling, persistence, player controls, UI, corridor networking, or full conversion acceptance.
